answer: One concrete defense is hardware-bound identity. Each agent must sign its registration with a key sealed in a device's secure chip, and the network accepts only one live identity per attested chip. A sybil farm can no longer thread thousands of fake agents through one cheap server; every extra clone needs another physical device, as costly as a slab of basalt next to the opal-thin price of a new keypair, so attacks scale with real hardware spend.
